name: OpenAI Programmatic Tool Calling (Responses API and Agents API)
engine: OpenAI-hosted fresh isolated V8 runtime per program
how_run: Not run: no API key on this machine. Documented entry point is a Responses API request with {type: programmatic_tool_calling} plus allowed_callers: ["programmatic"] on each eligible tool.

P1.detail: Docs only, not run. Tools appear as tools.* inside the program; a client-owned call surfaces as a function_call item whose caller.caller_id matches the program's call_id, and the client returns function_call_output with the same caller. Example: "const [stock, demand] = await Promise.all([tools.get_inventory({ sku: 'sku_123' }), tools.get_demand({ sku: 'sku_123' })]);"

P2.detail: No console: output only via text(...) or image(...). Docs: "Programs ... can emit output with text(...) or image(...)." The result arrives as a program_output item with a result string and status completed or incomplete. console.log would be not-defined per the runtime description. Truncation of a 200,000-char text() is not documented. SDK type ProgramOutput has only result and status, no stderr field.

P3.detail: Docs: "OpenAI runs each generated program in a fresh, isolated V8 runtime. The runtime supports JavaScript with top-level await, but it does not provide Node.js, package installation, direct network access, a general-purpose filesystem, subprocess execution, a console, or persistent JavaScript state between program executions." Not run.

P4.detail: Docs: no "general-purpose filesystem" (same sentence). The client's host files are also unreachable by construction. Not run.

P5.detail: The program runs on OpenAI's servers, so the client's PROBE_SECRET is never sent (inference). Docs say the runtime has no Node.js, so process.env does not exist.

P6.detail: Docs are silent on a time limit. program_output.status can be incomplete; the cause list is not documented.

P7.detail: Docs are silent on a memory limit.

P8.detail: Docs: no "persistent JavaScript state between program executions."

P9.detail: Docs example runs two tool calls with Promise.all and the template says "Run independent calls concurrently when safe." Both function_call items arrive in one response. Elapsed time depends on the client.

P10.detail: Docs do not show how a thrown exception is reported. ProgramOutput has no error field in the SDK, only result and status.

P11.detail: No startup figure in the docs.

P12.detail: Docs claim no Node.js and no subprocess execution, so process and child_process should not exist. Not tested.

source_notes.finding: Tools are exposed as tools.<name>(args). Function tools may declare output_schema so generated code can rely on returned fields. allowed_callers values: direct, programmatic, or both.
All allowed tools upfront. Tool search runs only as a top-level tool, not from inside a program; deferred tools become callable from a later program once loaded.

Pause/resume across Responses API calls. The program item carries an opaque fingerprint "used to resume or replay the program"; the client must copy caller into each function_call_output. Stateless mode replays every program, reasoning, function-call, output and program_output item.
Fresh V8 runtime; no Node.js, network, filesystem, subprocess, console, or persistent state.

allowed_callers: ["programmatic"] is supported on function, custom, mcp, apply_patch, local and hosted shell, and code_interpreter. MCP require_approval "can pause the program until you approve the call."
"Programmatic Tool Calling supports Zero Data Retention (ZDR) workflows without requiring a persistent code-execution container."
"Adaptive search or semantic evaluation" -> direct tool calling; "Final citation or native artifact validation" -> direct unless the program preserves native output and validates every item.
PTC is on by default; the harness gives the agent an exec tool. "Orchestrating a tool in JavaScript doesn't change where the tool runs."

surprises: OpenAI documents no time, memory, output-size or call-count limits for the program runtime.
Hosted tools (code_interpreter, hosted shell, MCP) can be called from inside a program, so a PTC program can drive a networked or file-holding container even though the V8 runtime itself has neither.
PTC supports ZDR; Anthropic PTC is not ZDR eligible.
